study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Lin et al., Journal of Affective Disorders, 2023
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Understanding the heterogeneity of dynamic functional connectivity patterns in first-episode drug naïve depression using normative models

detail.IBCDR: International Big-Data Center for Depression Research

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: We employed data from International Big-Data Center for Depression Research

answer.IBCDR: healthy-ICA group to construct brain networks; healthy-base group to build normative model; healthy-comparison group for case-control comparison with FEDN-MDD patients

detail.healthy-ICA: used to construct group-level brain networks (GIG-ICA guidance)
detail.healthy-base: used to construct the sex-specific normative age model
detail.healthy-comparison: used for comparison with FEDN-MDD group

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: The data from the healthy-ICA group were only used to construct the brain networks (as shown in Fig. 1, the purple figures). The data from the healthy-base group were used to construct the sex-specific normative age model (as shown in Fig. 1, the blue figures). And the comparison was made between the healthy-comparison group and the FEDN-MDD group.

model-1.model-name: normative model for dynamic characteristics (healthy-base group)
model-1.train-phase: 90% of 289 per fold (10-fold CV; exact N not stated)

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: Healthy-base controls (N=289) were used to establish the normative model; 10-fold cross-validation trained on 90% each fold.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: Another 289 healthy control individuals (165 female, as a healthy-base group) of 832 controls were included to establish a normative model; We repeatedly trained the polynomial regression model on 90 % of the 289 healthybase participants, withholding the remaining 10 % for estimating generalization performance.
